claims.claim: Marley, Scrooge's partner, is dead, and Scrooge signed the burial register
claims.evidence: 'Marley was dead: to begin with... The register of his burial was signed... Scrooge signed it'

claims.claim: Scrooge is a tight-fisted old moneylender
claims.evidence: Searched moneylend/usur/loan/banker: text calls him 'squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner' with a counting-house and a banker's-book; no moneylending

claims.claim: Scrooge spends Christmas Eve in his counting-house refusing his nephew and the charity collectors
claims.evidence: 'old Scrooge sat busy in his counting-house'; 'Provision for the Poor and destitute'; nephew's invitation refused

claims.claim: Scrooge rebuffs Fred and grudges Bob Cratchit Christmas Day off
claims.evidence: 'I suppose you must have the whole day. Be here all the more early next morning'

claims.claim: Marley's ghost warns him of three spirits
claims.evidence: Marley's Ghost announces the spirits in Stave One

claims.claim: Ghost of Christmas Past shows his lonely youth and Fezziwig's ball
claims.evidence: 'a lonely boy was reading near a feeble fire'; 'Mr. Fezziwig's Ball'

claims.claim: Ghost of Christmas Present shows the Cratchits' dinner and the sickly Tiny Tim
claims.evidence: 'Tiny Tim upon his shoulder. Alas for Tiny Tim, he bore a little crutch, and had his limbs supported by an iron frame!'

claims.claim: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows Tiny Tim's death and Scrooge's own grave
claims.evidence: 'The colour? Ah, poor Tiny Tim!'; 'read upon the stone of the neglected grave his own name, Ebenezer Scrooge'

claims.claim: Scrooge wakes reformed, sends a prize turkey to the Cratchits, joins Fred's party, raises Bob's salary, and is a second father to Tiny Tim
claims.evidence: 'the prize Turkey'; 'I am about to raise your salary!'; 'to Tiny Tim, who did not die, he was a second father'

claims.claim: Tiny Tim is Cratchit's youngest son
claims.evidence: No statement of birth order found
claims.fix: sickly little son, who walks with a crutch

claims.claim: Fezziwig is Scrooge's old master; Fred cheerful nephew; Bob Cratchit clerk
claims.evidence: 'it's old Fezziwig! Bless his heart; it's Fezziwig alive again!' (Scrooge apprenticed to him)
